literature.headline_zh: 人肠道病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期人肠道病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: Jun13133在新生小鼠模型中表现出良好的体内药代动力学特性,并减轻了瘫痪,防止了体重减轻,减少了脊髓和肌肉组织中的病毒复制。 [10.1021/acs.jmedchem.6c00818]
然而,其保护作用主要针对特定型别,无法可靠地扩展到主要的非EV-A71肠道病毒,如柯萨奇病毒A16(CVA16)、CVA6或CVA10。 [10.3390/vaccines14100842]
化合物X14通过抑制病毒复制显示出强效的抗EV71活性,并对代表性的EV-A、EV-B、EV-C和EV-D肠道病毒表现出广谱活性。它还显示出优于母体化合物的体内疗效。 [10.1021/acs.jmedchem.6c01273]
波形蛋白的敲除显著抑制了BHK-21细胞中FMDV的复制。使用IDPN和丙烯酰胺处理的治疗破坏了波形蛋白的结构重排并抑制了FMDV复制。FMDV上调CaMKIIγ的表达,导致波形蛋白在Ser39和Ser83位点的磷酸化。 [10.1016/j.vetmic.2026.111228]
在三个年度采样组中,辛普森多样性指数与采样年份呈显著负相关。人类星状病毒1占最大比例,且获得了与肠外感染相关的星状病毒MLB2几乎完整的基因组序列。 [10.3389/fmicb.2026.1966428]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Jun13133 demonstrated favorable in vivo pharmacokinetic properties and mitigated paralysis, prevented weight loss, and reduced viral replication in spinal cord and muscle tissues in the neonatal mouse model. [10.1021/acs.jmedchem.6c00818]
Their protection, however, is predominantly type-specific and does not extend reliably to major non-EV-A71 enteroviruses such as coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16), CVA6, or CVA10. [10.3390/vaccines14100842]

Anhui reported 1,292,579 HFMD cases from 2008 to 2023, including 47,990 (3.7%) typed cases. EV71 declined from 45.8% (8479/18,534) of typed cases before vaccine introduction to 3.4% (578/16,930) during the COVID-19 pandemic, while other enteroviruses increased from 29.6% (5487/18,534) to 81.8% (13,848/16,930). [10.2196/99663]

Compound X14 showed strong anti-EV71 activity by inhibiting viral replication and demonstrated broad-spectrum activity against representative EV-A, EV-B, EV-C, and EV-D enteroviruses. It also exhibited superior in vivo efficacy compared to the parent compound. [10.1021/acs.jmedchem.6c01273]

Knockout of vimentin significantly suppressed FMDV replication in BHK-21 cells. Treatment with IDPN and acrylamide disrupted vimentin structural rearrangement and inhibited FMDV replication. FMDV upregulates CaMKIIγ expression, leading to vimentin phosphorylation at Ser39 and Ser83. [10.1016/j.vetmic.2026.111228]

papers.title: From Monovalent EV-A71 Vaccines to Multivalent Vaccines Against Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease in China: Development Progress, Evidence Gaps, and Translational Challenges
papers.abstract: Hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) is caused by several enteroviruses, with enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) most strongly associated with severe disease and death. Licensed monovalent inactivated EV-A71 vaccines in China have a substantial evidence base for safety, immunogenicity, protective efficacy, and real-world effectiveness, together with relatively mature clinical evaluation and quality control systems. Their protection, however, is predominantly type-specific and does not extend reliably to major non-EV-A71 enteroviruses such as coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16), CVA6, or CVA10. As EV-A71-associated disease has declined, these viruses have become more prominent among residual cases and outbreaks, although shifts in etiological proportions should not be equated with vaccine-driven type replacement. This review synthesizes evidence on the developmental basis and limits of monovalent EV-A71 vaccination and evaluates multivalent candidates based on inactivated virus, virus-like particles (VLPs), chimeric antigens, and nucleic acid platforms. Most multivalent evidence remains preclinical, and major translational gaps include the absence of population-validated correlates of protection for non-EV-A71 types, uncertain antigenic coverage, component-specific quality control requirements, immune response imbalance, clinical case accrual, pediatric safety, coadministration, and affordability. We therefore propose a stage-gated framework that separates developmental maturity from public health priority and evaluates each additional antigen according to product objectives, sustained absolute disease burden, antigenic coverage, manufacturing readiness, immune response balance, clinical evaluability, and incremental public health value. Under this framework, higher valency is a conditional development choice rather than an objective in itself, and vaccine composition should be adapted to regional epidemiology and measurable added benefit over lower valency comparators.

analysis.scope_and_question: Hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) is caused by several enteroviruses, with enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) most strongly associated with severe disease and death.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Licensed monovalent inactivated EV-A71 vaccines in China have a substantial evidence base for safety, immunogenicity, protective efficacy, and real-world effectiveness, together with relatively mature clinical evaluation and quality control systems.

analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: As EV-A71-associated disease has declined, these viruses have become more prominent among residual cases and outbreaks, although shifts in etiological proportions should not be equated with vaccine-driven type replacement.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on the development and evaluation of monovalent and multivalent vaccines against human enteroviruses, particularly EV-A71, which is strongly associated with severe Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease (HFMD). The evidence highlights the substantial safety, immunogenicity, and effectiveness of monovalent EV-A71 vaccines in China, but notes their limited protection against other enteroviruses like CVA16, CVA6, and CVA10. The review emphasizes the need for multivalent vaccine strategies to address the increasing role of non-EV-A71 viruses in HFMD outbreaks. However, most multivalent evidence remains preclinical, and key challenges include the lack of population-validated correlates of protection, uncertain antigenic coverage, and issues with quality control and affordability. The paper proposes a stage-gated framework for evaluating multivalent vaccine development, prioritizing public health value and regional epidemiology over valency alone.

papers.title_zh: 从单价EV-A71 疫苗到多价疫苗应对中国手足口病:研发进展、证据缺口与转化挑战
papers.source_body_en: Hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) is caused by several enteroviruses, with enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) most strongly associated with severe disease and death. Licensed monovalent inactivated EV-A71 vaccines in China have a substantial evidence base for safety, immunogenicity, protective efficacy, and real-world effectiveness, together with relatively mature clinical evaluation and quality control systems. Their protection, however, is predominantly type-specific and does not extend reliably to major non-EV-A71 enteroviruses such as coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16), CVA6, or CVA10. As EV-A71-associated disease has declined, these viruses have become more prominent among residual cases and outbreaks, although shifts in etiological proportions should not be equated with vaccine-driven type replacement. This review synthesizes evidence on the developmental basis and limits of monovalent EV-A71 vaccination and evaluates multivalent candidates based on inactivated virus, virus-like particles (VLPs), chimeric antigens, and nucleic acid platforms. Most multivalent evidence remains preclinical, and major translational gaps include the absence of population-validated correlates of protection for non-EV-A71 types, uncertain antigenic coverage, component-specific quality control requirements, immune response imbalance, clinical case accrual, pediatric safety, coadministration, and affordability. We therefore propose a stage-gated framework that separates developmental maturity from public health priority and evaluates each additional antigen according to product objectives, sustained absolute disease burden, antigenic coverage, manufacturing readiness, immune response balance, clinical evaluability, and incremental public health value. Under this framework, higher valency is a conditional development choice rather than an objective in itself, and vaccine composition should be adapted to regional epidemiology and measurable added benefit over lower valency comparators.
papers.abstract_zh: 手足口病(HFMD)由多种肠道病毒引起,其中肠道病毒A71(EV-A71)与严重疾病和死亡最为相关。在中国,已获批的单价灭活EV-A71 疫苗具有充分的安全性、免疫原性、保护效力和实际效果的证据基础,同时具备相对成熟的临床评估和质量控制体系。然而,其保护作用主要针对特定型别,无法可靠地扩展到主要的非EV-A71肠道病毒,如柯萨奇病毒A16(CVA16)、CVA6或CVA10。随着EV-A71相关病例的减少,这些病毒在剩余病例和暴发中变得更加突出,尽管病原体比例的变化不应等同于由疫苗驱动的型别替代。本综述总结了单价EV-A71 疫苗接种的研发基础和局限性,并基于灭活病毒、病毒样颗粒(VLPs)、嵌合抗原和核酸平台评估多价候选疫苗。目前大多数多价证据仍处于临床前阶段,主要的转化缺口包括缺乏对非EV-A71型别的群体验证的保护相关指标、抗原覆盖范围不确定、成分特异性质量控制要求、免疫应答失衡、临床病例积累、儿童安全性、联合接种以及可负担性。因此,我们提出一个分阶段框架,将研发成熟度与公共卫生优先级分开,并根据产品目标、持续的绝对疾病负担、抗原覆盖范围、制造准备度、免疫应答平衡、临床可评估性以及增量公共卫生价值来评估每种额外抗原。在该框架下,更高的价型是一种有条件的研发选择,而非其本身的目标,疫苗的组成应根据地区流行病学和相对于低价对照品的可衡量附加效益进行调整。

papers.title: Development of Enterovirus D68 3C Protease Inhibitors with In Vivo Efficacy in a Neurological Infection Model
papers.abstract: Abstract Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a non-polio enterovirus that primarily causes respiratory illness but can also lead to severe disease, including acute flaccid myelitis. No approved vaccine or antiviral is available. Here, we report the rational design and structure−property optimization of dipeptidyl EV-D68 3C protease (3Cpro) inhibitors. Structure-guided optimization and prodrug modification identified Jun13133 as a potent antiviral active against multiple contemporary EV-D68 isolates and EV-A71, with high selectivity. Computational modeling supported a stable substrate-mimetic binding mode consistent with reported covalent 3Cpro inhibitors. Jun13133 also showed favorable in vivo pharmacokinetic properties. In a neonatal mouse model of EV-D68-induced neurological disease, Jun13133 mitigated paralysis, prevented weight loss, and reduced viral replication in spinal cord and muscle tissues. These results validate EV-D68 3Cpro as a druggable antiviral target and support Jun13133 as a promising lead for further development.

Structure-guided optimization and prodrug modification identified Jun13133 as a potent antiviral active against multiple contemporary EV-D68 isolates and EV-A71, with high selectivity. Computational modeling supported a stable substrate-mimetic binding mode consistent with reported covalent 3Cpro inhibitors. Jun13133 also showed favorable in vivo pharmacokinetic properties. In a neonatal mouse model of EV-D68-induced neurological disease, Jun13133 mitigated paralysis, prevented weight loss, and reduced viral replication in spinal cord and muscle tissues. These results validate EV-D68 3Cpro as a druggable antiviral target and support Jun13133 as a promising lead for further development.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及二肽类EV-D68 3C蛋白酶抑制剂的合理设计和优化,并在EV-D68诱导的神经疾病新生小鼠模型中测试其体内疗效。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究验证了EV-D68 3Cpro作为可药用靶点的潜力,并确定了Jun13133作为进一步开发的有前景的先导化合物,突显了这种方法在治疗EV-D68感染中的应用前景。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为开发针对EV-D68的抗病毒药物治疗方案提供信息,该病毒可导致严重的神经并发症,并支持Jun13133作为潜在的抗病毒药物选项。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括使用新生小鼠模型,这可能无法完全代表人类疾病,以及需要进一步的临床验证Jun13133。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 Enterovirus D68(EV-D68)是一种非脊髓灰质炎肠道病毒,主要引起呼吸道疾病,但也可能导致严重疾病,包括急性弛缓性脊髓炎。目前尚无获批的抗病毒药物或治疗方案用于该非脊髓灰质炎肠道病毒。本文报告了针对EV-D68 3C蛋白酶(3Cpro)的二肽类抑制剂的合理设计和结构-性质优化。结构指导的优化和前药修饰确定了Jun13133,这是一种对多种当前EV-D68分离株和EV-A71具有高选择性的强效抗病毒药物。计算建模支持了该抑制剂稳定的底物模拟结合模式,与已报道的共价3Cpro抑制剂一致。Jun13133还表现出良好的体内药代动力学特性。在EV-D68诱导的神经疾病新生小鼠模型中,Jun13133减轻了瘫痪,防止了体重减轻,并减少了脊髓和肌肉组织中的病毒复制。这些结果验证了EV-D68 3Cpro作为可药用治疗靶点的潜力,并支持Jun13133作为进一步开发的有前景的先导化合物。

papers.title: Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease Surveillance in Anhui, After Introduction of the Enterovirus 71 Vaccine and During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Ecological Interrupted Time Series Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Routine surveillance is important for understanding hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) after monovalent enterovirus 71 (EV71) vaccine introduction, but interpretation is difficult when etiologic typing is sparse and the COVID-19 pandemic overlaps with the postvaccine era. OBJECTIVE: This study described surveillance-derived changes in HFMD burden and typed serotype composition in Anhui Province, China, after EV71 vaccine introduction and during the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective ecological surveillance study using HFMD records from January 2008 to December 2023. The primary analysis used negative-binomial interrupted time series (ITS) counterfactual models for all reported HFMD cases and typed EV71 monthly counts. Vaccine-era models were trained using data from January 2013 through May 2016; the previous specification covering January 2010 through May 2016 was retained as a sensitivity analysis. COVID-19-period models were trained using data from January 2008 through December 2019. Secondary analyses assessed spatial, temporal, and age patterns. Vaccine coverage histories, individual vaccination records, specimen submission metadata, and laboratory platform-change metadata were unavailable; therefore, models estimated calendar-based surveillance deviations rather than vaccine effectiveness. RESULTS: Anhui reported 1,292,579 HFMD cases from 2008 to 2023, including 47,990 (3.7%) typed cases. EV71 declined from 45.8% (8479/18,534) of typed cases before vaccine introduction to 3.4% (578/16,930) during COVID-19, while other enteroviruses increased from 29.6% (5487/18,534) to 81.8% (13,848/16,930). There were 123 deaths from 2008 to 2023, corresponding to 9.52 deaths per 100,000 reported cases; no deaths were recorded from 2020 to 2023. In primary vaccine-era ITS models, typed EV71 counts remained below the predicted trajectory in 2017 to 2019: 470 observed vs 659 predicted cases (95% prediction interval [PI] 467-933) in 2017, 181 vs 531 (95% PI 379-798) in 2018, and 63 vs 427 (95% PI 305-662) in 2019. All reported HFMD cases were not uniformly below the vaccine-era counterfactual. During the COVID-19 pandemic, all reported HFMD cases remained below prediction through 2023, with the largest relative difference in 2022 (28,385 observed vs 175,601 predicted; 95% PI 111,465-268,202). The proportion of reported children aged ≥4 years increased from 19% (50,503/266,132) during 2017 to 2019 to 29.1% (44,133/151,795) during 2021 to 2023 (odds ratio 1.75, 95% CI 1.72-1.78; P<.001). CONCLUSIONS: Typed EV71 surveillance signals declined after EV71 vaccine introduction, and overall HFMD burden was strongly disrupted during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, sparse typing, unavailable vaccination and testing policy metadata, and the aggregated other enteroviruses category limit causal interpretation. These findings should be read as surveillance signals, not as direct estimates of population-level serotype replacement or individual-level vaccine protection.

papers.abstract_original: BACKGROUND: Routine surveillance is important for understanding hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) after monovalent enterovirus 71 (EV71) vaccine introduction, but interpretation is difficult when etiologic typing is sparse and the COVID-19 pandemic overlaps with the postvaccine era. OBJECTIVE: This study described surveillance-derived changes in HFMD burden and typed serotype composition in Anhui Province, China, after EV71 vaccine introduction and during the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective ecological surveillance study using HFMD records from January 2008 to December 2023. The primary analysis used negative-binomial interrupted time series (ITS) counterfactual models for all reported HFMD cases and typed EV71 monthly counts. Vaccine-era models were trained using data from January 2013 through May 2016; the previous specification covering January 2010 through May 2016 was retained as a sensitivity analysis. COVID-19-period models were trained using data from January 2008 through December 2019. Secondary analyses assessed spatial, temporal, and age patterns. Vaccine coverage histories, individual vaccination records, specimen submission metadata, and laboratory platform-change metadata were unavailable; therefore, models estimated calendar-based surveillance deviations rather than vaccine effectiveness. RESULTS: Anhui reported 1,292,579 HFMD cases from 2008 to 2023, including 47,990 (3.7%) typed cases. EV71 declined from 45.8% (8479/18,534) of typed cases before vaccine introduction to 3.4% (578/16,930) during COVID-19, while other enteroviruses increased from 29.6% (5487/18,534) to 81.8% (13,848/16,930). There were 123 deaths from 2008 to 2023, corresponding to 9.52 deaths per 100,000 reported cases; no deaths were recorded from 2020 to 2023. In primary vaccine-era ITS models, typed EV71 counts remained below the predicted trajectory in 2017 to 2019: 470 observed vs 659 predicted cases (95% prediction interval [PI] 467-933) in 2017, 181 vs 531 (95% PI 379-798) in 2018, and 63 vs 427 (95% PI 305-662) in 2019. All reported HFMD cases were not uniformly below the vaccine-era counterfactual. During the COVID-19 pandemic, all reported HFMD cases remained below prediction through 2023, with the largest relative difference in 2022 (28,385 observed vs 175,601 predicted; 95% PI 111,465-268,202). The proportion of reported children aged ≥4 years increased from 19% (50,503/266,132) during 2017 to 2019 to 29.1% (44,133/151,795) during 2021 to 2023 (odds ratio 1.75, 95% CI 1.72-1.78; P<.001). CONCLUSIONS: Typed EV71 surveillance signals declined after EV71 vaccine introduction, and overall HFMD burden was strongly disrupted during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, sparse typing, unavailable vaccination and testing policy metadata, and the aggregated other enteroviruses category limit causal interpretation. These findings should be read as surveillance signals, not as direct estimates of population-level serotype replacement or individual-level vaccine protection.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed changes in hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) burden and serotype composition in Anhui Province, China, after the introduction of the monovalent enterovirus 71 (EV71) vaccine and during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using ecological surveillance data from 2008 to 2023, the researchers applied interrupted time series (ITS) models to assess the impact of the vaccine and pandemic on HFMD cases. They found a significant decline in EV71 cases and an increase in other enteroviruses, with overall HFMD burden strongly disrupted during the pandemic. The study highlights the importance of surveillance in understanding disease dynamics but notes limitations in causal interpretation due to sparse typing and lack of detailed vaccination data. These findings can inform public health strategies for HFMD monitoring and response during future outbreaks.

papers.title: Virucidal Efficacy of Holder Pasteurization of Breast Milk in a Portable Device
papers.abstract: Breast milk is the optimal nutrition for infants. However, a number of viruses can accumulate in breast milk and be transmitted to a newborn during breastfeeding. Holder pasteurization is a gold-standard method for breast milk treatment, achieving an acceptable compromise between microbiological safety and biological quality. We have evaluated the virucidal activity of Holder pasteurization of breast milk contaminated with RNA and DNA viruses in a portable home-use pasteurizer. Viruses were selected on basis of their ability to infect humans, contaminate breast milk, and pose a threat for a newborn. The efficacy was evaluated in experimental conditions using breast milk samples from four different donors. Infectious virus and viral genome content were assessed. Holder pasteurization resulted in a decrease in infectivity below the detection limit for enveloped RNA viruses (HIV-1, CHIKV, and SARS-CoV-2), but not RSV, and a partial decrease in infectious virus titer for non-enveloped RNA enteroviruses (EV-A71, E30, and PV1), and DNA viruses (hAdV5 and HSV-1). Moreover, infectivity reduction in E30 and PV1 in different samples of breast milk significantly differed. Therefore, Holder pasteurization can be a tool in the novel pandemic preparedness toolbox or probably help mothers manage breastfeeding during common infections.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the virucidal efficacy of Holder pasteurization of breast milk in a portable device to address the risk of virus transmission through breastfeeding. The background highlights the importance of breast milk as optimal nutrition for infants and the potential for viruses to contaminate it, posing a threat to newborns.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated the efficacy of Holder pasteurization using breast milk samples from four different donors in a portable home-use pasteurizer. The design focused on assessing the reduction of infectious virus and viral genome content for various viruses, including RNA and DNA viruses.
analysis.methods: The methods involved assessing infectious virus and viral genome content before and after Holder pasteurization of breast milk contaminated with RNA and DNA viruses. The study used a portable home-use pasteurizer to evaluate the virucidal activity of the process.
analysis.main_results: Holder pasteurization resulted in a decrease in infectivity below the detection limit for enveloped RNA viruses (HIV-1, CHIKV, and SARS-CoV-2), but not RSV, and a partial decrease in infectious virus titer for non-enveloped RNA enteroviruses (EV-A71, E30, and PV1), and DNA viruses (hAdV5 and HSV-1).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that Holder pasteurization can be a tool in the novel pandemic preparedness toolbox or help mothers manage breastfeeding during common infections, highlighting the partial efficacy against non-enveloped RNA enteroviruses and DNA viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that Holder pasteurization can reduce the risk of virus transmission through breast milk, which is significant for public health, especially during viral outbreaks or common infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of a limited number of breast milk samples from four donors, which may affect generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited sample size and the need for further validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the virucidal efficacy of Holder pasteurization of breast milk in a portable device, demonstrating significant reduction in infectivity for enveloped RNA viruses and partial reduction for non-enveloped RNA enteroviruses and DNA viruses. The findings suggest potential use in pandemic preparedness and managing breastfeeding during infections.

The background highlights the importance of breast milk as optimal nutrition for infants and the potential for viruses to contaminate it, posing a threat to newborns.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated the efficacy of Holder pasteurization using breast milk samples from four different donors in a portable home-use pasteurizer. The design focused on assessing the reduction of infectious virus and viral genome content for various viruses, including RNA and DNA viruses.
elements_en.methods: The methods involved assessing infectious virus and viral genome content before and after Holder pasteurization of breast milk contaminated with RNA and DNA viruses. The study used a portable home-use pasteurizer to evaluate the virucidal activity of the process.
elements_en.main_results: Holder pasteurization resulted in a decrease in infectivity below the detection limit for enveloped RNA viruses (HIV-1, CHIKV, and SARS-CoV-2), but not RSV, and a partial decrease in infectious virus titer for non-enveloped RNA enteroviruses (EV-A71, E30, and PV1), and DNA viruses (hAdV5 and HSV-1).
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that Holder pasteurization can be a tool in the novel pandemic preparedness toolbox or help mothers manage breastfeeding during common infections, highlighting the partial efficacy against non-enveloped RNA enteroviruses and DNA viruses.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that Holder pasteurization can reduce the risk of virus transmission through breast milk, which is significant for public health, especially during viral outbreaks or common infections.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of a limited number of breast milk samples from four donors, which may affect generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited sample size and the need for further validation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估Holder巴氏杀菌法在便携式设备中对母乳的病毒灭活效果,以应对通过哺乳传播病毒传播的风险。背景强调了母乳作为婴儿最佳营养的重要性,以及病毒可能污染母乳并威胁新生儿的潜在风险。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用便携式家用巴氏杀菌设备评估了Holder巴氏杀菌法的效果,评估对象为来自四位不同供体的母乳样本。研究设计侧重于评估各种病毒(包括RNA和DNA病毒)的感染性病毒和病毒基因组含量的减少情况。
elements_zh.methods: 方法包括在Holder巴氏杀菌前后评估含有RNA和DNA病毒的母乳中的感染性病毒和病毒基因组含量。研究使用便携式家用巴氏杀菌设备来评估该过程的病毒灭活活性。
elements_zh.main_results: Holder巴氏杀菌法对包膜RNA病毒(HIV-1、CHIKV和SARS-CoV-2)的感染性降低了至检测限以下,但对RSV无效,并且对非包膜RNA肠道病毒(EV-A71、E30和PV1)以及DNA病毒(hAdV5和HSV-1)的感染性滴度产生了部分降低。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为Holder巴氏杀菌法可以成为新型大流行病防控工具箱中的工具,或者帮助母亲在常见感染期间管理哺乳,强调了其对非包膜RNA肠道病毒和DNA病毒的部分有效性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,Holder巴氏杀菌法可以降低通过母乳传播病毒传播的风险,这对公共卫生具有重要意义,尤其是在病毒暴发暴发或常见感染期间。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括仅使用四位供体的有限数量母乳样本,这可能影响结果的普遍适用性。由于样本量有限以及需要进一步验证,证据强度为中等。

papers.title_zh: Holder巴氏杀菌法在便携式设备中对母乳的病毒灭活效果
papers.source_body_en: Breast milk is the optimal nutrition for infants. However, a number of viruses can accumulate in breast milk and be transmitted to a newborn during breastfeeding. Holder pasteurization is a gold-standard method for breast milk treatment, achieving an acceptable compromise between microbiological safety and biological quality. We have evaluated the virucidal activity of Holder pasteurization of breast milk contaminated with RNA and DNA viruses in a portable home-use pasteurizer. Viruses were selected on basis of their ability to infect humans, contaminate breast milk, and pose a threat for a newborn. The efficacy was evaluated in experimental conditions using breast milk samples from four different donors. Infectious virus and viral genome content were assessed. Holder pasteurization resulted in a decrease in infectivity below the detection limit for enveloped RNA viruses (HIV-1, CHIKV, and SARS-CoV-2), but not RSV, and a partial decrease in infectious virus titer for non-enveloped RNA enteroviruses (EV-A71, E30, and PV1), and DNA viruses (hAdV5 and HSV-1). Moreover, infectivity reduction in E30 and PV1 in different samples of breast milk significantly differed. Therefore, Holder pasteurization can be a tool in the novel pandemic preparedness toolbox or probably help mothers manage breastfeeding during common infections.
papers.abstract_zh: 母乳是婴儿的最佳营养来源。然而,一些病毒可能在母乳中积累,并通过哺乳传播给新生儿。Holder巴氏杀菌法是母乳灭活病毒的标准方法,在微生物安全性和生物活性之间取得可接受的平衡。我们评估了Holder巴氏杀菌法在便携式家用巴氏杀菌设备中对含有RNA和DNA病毒的母乳的病毒灭活效果。所选病毒基于其能够感染人类、污染母乳以及对新生儿构成威胁的能力。在实验条件下,使用来自四位不同供体的母乳样本评估了病毒的灭活效果。评估了感染性病毒和病毒基因组含量。Holder巴氏杀菌法对包膜RNA病毒(HIV-1、CHIKV和SARS-CoV-2)的感染性降低了至检测限以下,但对RSV无效,并且对非包膜RNA肠道病毒(EV-A71、E30和PV1)以及DNA病毒(hAdV5和HSV-1)的感染性滴度产生了部分降低。此外,不同母乳样本中E30和PV1的感染性降低程度存在显著差异。因此,Holder巴氏杀菌法可以成为新型大流行病防控工具箱中的工具,或者帮助母亲在常见感染期间管理哺乳。

papers.title: High-throughput sequencing reveals the virome characteristics of wastewater in Gansu Province, China from 2024 to 2026
papers.abstract: Emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases continue to pose a persistent challenge to global public health security. As an unbiased and noninvasive population-level surveillance approach, wastewater-based epidemiology has emerged as an urban-scale monitoring tool for proactively capturing the community disease burden. In this study, metagenomic and targeted next-generation sequencing were employed to preliminarily characterize wastewater viral communities in Gansu Province from 2024 to 2026. Across the three annual sampling groups, the Simpson diversity index calculated from metagenomic taxonomic profiles showed a significant negative correlation with sampling year. Despite viral enrichment, more than 97% of sequencing reads were assigned to bacteria, likely reflecting residual nonviral nucleic acids and limitations in metagenomic classification. The wastewater virome exhibited a complex host-association spectrum, within which bacteriophages and plant-associated viruses displayed relatively stable community structures and high relative abundances. Among human pathogens, astroviruses were consistently detected at high relative abundances across all samples. Human astrovirus 1 accounted for the largest proportion, and a nearly complete genome sequence of the extraintestinal infection-associated astrovirus MLB2 was recovered. Targeted sequencing further revealed a highly structured environmental enterovirus profile dominated by the species Enterovirus betacoxsackie , followed by Enterovirus alphacoxsackie , whereas Enterovirus coxsackiepol was detected at an extremely low abundance and Enterovirus deconjuncti was not detected. In addition to several common viruses associated with hand, foot, and mouth disease, rare viruses, including coxsackievirus A19 and enterovirus B83, were successfully captured. Echovirus 11 was identified as the predominant enterovirus serotype in current wastewater surveillance in Gansu Province. In summary, this study provides a preliminary characterization of the viral community profiles in wastewater samples from Gansu Province, demonstrates the effectiveness of wastewater-based epidemiology for population-level surveillance, and underscores the need to establish a coordinated defense network integrating clinical case surveillance with environmental monitoring.

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the potential presence of residual nonviral nucleic acids and the challenges in metagenomic classification, which may affect the accuracy of viral community characterization. The results showed a significant negative correlation between the Simpson diversity index and the sampling year, with human astrovirus 1 being the most prevalent. A nearly complete genome sequence of the extraintestinal infection-associated astrovirus MLB2 was recovered. The study identified echovirus 11 as the predominant enterovirus serotype in wastewater surveillance, which has implications for public health. However, limitations include the potential presence of residual nonviral nucleic acids and challenges in metagenomic classification, which may affect the accuracy of findings. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases continue to pose a persistent challenge to global public health security. The study aimed to characterize the virome of wastewater in Gansu Province, China, to better understand the community disease burden.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This study employed metagenomic and targeted next-generation sequencing to analyze wastewater samples collected from Gansu Province between 2024 and 2026. The population included wastewater samples from various locations in the province.
analysis_en.methods: Metagenomic and targeted next-generation sequencing were used to characterize the wastewater viral communities. Targeted sequencing further revealed a structured environmental enterovirus profile, with specific species identified based on their abundance.
analysis_en.main_results: Across the three annual sampling groups, the Simpson diversity index showed a significant negative correlation with the sampling year. Human astrovirus 1 accounted for the largest proportion, and a nearly complete genome sequence of the extraintestinal infection-associated astrovirus MLB2 was recovered.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified echovirus 11 as the predominant enterovirus serotype in current wastewater surveillance in Gansu Province, highlighting its potential role in community transmission.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into the prevalence and diversity of human enteroviruses in wastewater, which can inform public health strategies for surveillance and prevention of enterovirus-related diseases.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the potential presence of residual nonviral nucleic acids and the challenges in metagenomic classification, which may affect the accuracy of viral community characterization. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

papers.title_zh: 高通量测序揭示2024至2026年中国甘肃省污水中的病毒组特征
papers.source_body_en: Emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases continue to pose a persistent challenge to global public health security. As an unbiased and noninvasive population-level surveillance approach, wastewater-based epidemiology has emerged as an urban-scale monitoring tool for proactively capturing the community disease burden. In this study, metagenomic and targeted next-generation sequencing were employed to preliminarily characterize wastewater viral communities in Gansu Province from 2024 to 2026. Across the three annual sampling groups, the Simpson diversity index calculated from metagenomic taxonomic profiles showed a significant negative correlation with sampling year. Despite viral enrichment, more than 97% of sequencing reads were assigned to bacteria, likely reflecting residual nonviral nucleic acids and limitations in metagenomic classification. The wastewater virome exhibited a complex host-association spectrum, within which bacteriophages and plant-associated viruses displayed relatively stable community structures and high relative abundances. Among human pathogens, astroviruses were consistently detected at high relative abundances across all samples. Human astrovirus 1 accounted for the largest proportion, and a nearly complete genome sequence of the extraintestinal infection-associated astrovirus MLB2 was recovered. Targeted sequencing further revealed a highly structured environmental enterovirus profile dominated by the species Enterovirus betacoxsackie , followed by Enterovirus alphacoxsackie , whereas Enterovirus coxsackiepol was detected at an extremely low abundance and Enterovirus deconjuncti was not detected. In addition to several common viruses associated with hand, foot, and mouth disease, rare viruses, including coxsackievirus A19 and enterovirus B83, were successfully captured. Echovirus 11 was identified as the predominant enterovirus serotype in current wastewater surveillance in Gansu Province. In summary, this study provides a preliminary characterization of the viral community profiles in wastewater samples from Gansu Province, demonstrates the effectiveness of wastewater-based epidemiology for population-level surveillance, and underscores the need to establish a coordinated defense network integrating clinical case surveillance with environmental monitoring.
papers.abstract_zh: 新兴和再新兴传染病持续对全球公共卫生安全构成严峻挑战。作为一种无偏见且非侵入性的群体水平监测方法,基于污水的病毒组监测已成为城市规模主动捕捉社区疾病负担的工具。本研究采用宏基因组和靶向下一代测序技术,初步表征了2024至2026年中国甘肃省污水中的病毒群落。在三个年度采样组中,宏基因组分类谱计算出的辛普森多样性指数与采样年份呈显著负相关。尽管进行了病毒富集,超过97%的测序读段被归类为细菌,这可能反映了残留的非病毒核酸以及宏基因组分类的局限性。污水病毒组表现出复杂的病毒-宿主关联谱,其中噬菌体和植物相关病毒显示出相对稳定的群落结构和较高的相对丰度。在人类病原体中,星状病毒在所有样本中均被持续检测到,相对丰度较高。人类星状病毒1占最大比例,且获得了与肠外感染相关的星状病毒MLB2几乎完整的基因组序列。靶向测序进一步揭示了以肠病毒β-柯萨奇病毒为主导的结构化环境肠病毒谱,其次是肠病毒α-柯萨奇病毒,而肠病毒柯萨奇病毒B型则检测到极低丰度,肠病毒脱垂病毒则未被检测到。除了几种与手足口病相关的常见病毒外,还成功捕获了罕见病毒,包括柯萨奇病毒A19和肠病毒B83。研究确定肠病毒11是当前甘肃省污水中主要的肠病毒血清型,突显了其在社区传播中的潜在作用。总之,本研究初步表征了甘肃省污水样本中的病毒群落特征,展示了基于污水的病毒组监测在群体水平监测中的有效性,并强调了建立整合临床病例监测与环境监测的协调防御网络的必要性。

papers.title: CaMKIIγ-mediated vimentin structural rearrangement regulates FMDV replication.
papers.abstract: FMDV infection induces rearrangement of host cell membrane structures and recruits various proteins to form a replication complex for viral replication. Vimentin, a major component of type III intermediate filaments, has been implicated in the replication processes of multiple viruses. This study identifies that Vimentin interacts with FMDV 2 C and participates in replication complex formation. Knockout of Vimentin significantly suppressed FMDV replication in BHK-21 cells. FMDV infection did not affect Vimentin expression but instead induced the rearrangement of Vimentin network structure. Treatment with IDPN and acrylamide disrupted Vimentin structural rearrangement and inhibited FMDV replication. Furthermore, we demonstrated that FMDV upregulates CaMKIIγ expression, which in turn promotes Vimentin phosphorylation at Ser39 and Ser83 to induce structural rearrangement. Inhibiting CaMKIIγ activity resulted in a significant reduction in FMDV replication. Overexpression of Vimentin effectively enhanced the replication of several RNA viruses, including Poliovirus type 1, Enterovirus 71, Respiratory enteric orphan virus type 3 strain 176, Coxsackievirus A16, and Human parainfluenza virus type 2. Our results indicate that Vimentin regulates the replication of multiple RNA viruses, providing a theoretical reference for in-depth investigation into the mechanisms of RNA virus infection and the development of antiviral drugs.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the role of vimentin in FMDV replication and its interaction with viral proteins. The background highlights that FMDV infection induces host cell membrane rearrangements and recruits proteins to form a replication complex.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in BHK-21 cells, focusing on the interaction between FMDV and vimentin. It involved knockout experiments and treatment with specific compounds to assess their effects on viral replication.
analysis.methods: The methods included knockout of vimentin, treatment with IDPN and acrylamide, and overexpression of vimentin to evaluate its impact on FMDV replication. The study also demonstrated FMDV's ability to upregulate CaMKIIγ expression, which promotes vimentin phosphorylation.
analysis.main_results: Knockout of vimentin significantly suppressed FMDV replication in BHK-21 cells. Treatment with IDPN and acrylamide disrupted vimentin structural rearrangement and inhibited FMDV replication. FMDV upregulates CaMKIIγ expression, leading to vimentin phosphorylation at Ser39 and Ser83.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that vimentin structural rearrangement is a critical factor in FMDV replication, mediated by CaMKIIγ. This provides novel insights into the molecular mechanisms of RNA virus infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results offer a theoretical basis for understanding RNA virus replication mechanisms and could inform the development of antiviral strategies targeting vimentin and CaMKIIγ.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro experiments using BHK-21 cells, which may not fully represent in vivo conditions. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on cell culture findings without clinical validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the role of vimentin in FMDV replication, revealing that its structural rearrangement is essential for viral replication. The research identifies CaMKIIγ as a mediator of vimentin phosphorylation, which facilitates the formation of a replication complex. Knockout of vimentin and treatment with IDPN and acrylamide significantly inhibited FMDV replication, highlighting potential therapeutic targets. The findings provide novel insights into RNA virus infection mechanisms and suggest avenues for antiviral drug development. However, the study is limited to in vitro experiments, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on cell culture data without clinical application.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨波形蛋白在FMDV复制中的作用及其与病毒蛋白的相互作用。背景指出FMDV感染诱导了宿主细胞膜的重排,并招募蛋白质形成复制复合体。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在BHK-21细胞中进行,重点研究FMDV与波形蛋白的相互作用。研究涉及波形蛋白的敲除实验以及使用特定化合物的治疗处理,以评估其对病毒复制的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 方法包括波形蛋白的敲除、使用IDPN和丙烯酰胺的治疗处理,以及波形蛋白的过表达,以评估其对FMDV复制的影响。研究还证明了FMDV能够上调CaMKIIγ的表达,从而促进波形蛋白的磷酸化。
elements_zh.main_results: 波形蛋白的敲除显著抑制了BHK-21细胞中FMDV的复制。使用IDPN和丙烯酰胺处理的治疗破坏了波形蛋白的结构重排并抑制了FMDV复制。FMDV上调CaMKIIγ的表达,导致波形蛋白在Ser39和Ser83位点的磷酸化。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,波形蛋白结构重排是FMDV复制的关键因素,这一过程由CaMKIIγ介导。这为RNA病毒感染的分子机制提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为理解RNA病毒复制机制提供了理论基础,并可能为开发针对波形蛋白和CaMKIIγ的抗病毒药物抗病毒策略提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于在BHK-21细胞中进行的体外实验,可能无法完全代表体内情况。证据强度中等,因为其基于细胞培养结果,尚未经过临床验证。

papers.abstract_zh: FMDV感染诱导了宿主细胞膜结构的重排,并招募多种蛋白质形成复制复合体以进行病毒复制。波形蛋白是III型中间丝的主要成分,已被证实参与多种病毒的复制过程。本研究发现波形蛋白与FMDV 2C蛋白相互作用,并参与复制复合体的形成。波形蛋白的敲除显著抑制了BHK-21细胞中FMDV的复制。FMDV感染不影响波形蛋白的表达,但会诱导波形蛋白网络结构的重排。使用IDPN和丙烯酰胺处理的治疗破坏了波形蛋白的结构重排并抑制了FMDV复制。此外,我们证明FMDV上调CaMKIIγ的表达,进而促进波形蛋白在Ser39和Ser83位点的磷酸化,诱导结构重排。抑制CaMKIIγ活性显著降低了FMDV的复制。波形蛋白的过表达有效增强了多种RNA病毒的复制,包括脊髓灰质炎病毒1型、人肠道病毒71型、呼吸道肠道孤儿病毒3型176株、Coxsackievirus A16型和人副流感病毒2型。我们的结果表明波形蛋白调控多种RNA病毒的复制,为深入研究RNA病毒感染机制及开发抗病毒药物抗病毒药物提供了理论依据。

papers.title: A Bayesian modelling framework for inference of latent infection risk patterns from virus neutralisation assay titration data
papers.abstract: Serological assays remain the standard approach for estimating the cumulative incidence of a pathogen and monitoring population immunity. Titration data from virus neutralisation assays are conventionally analysed using a nearly century-old interpolation-based method that neglects inherent imperfections in the assay and produces estimates with no measure of uncertainty. We introduce a two-part Bayesian framework for inferring latent infection risk directly from raw titration data. First, we develop a mechanistic model for serum antibody titration data that estimates antibody concentrations while quantifying uncertainty. Second, we propagate this uncertainty into an age-structured sero-catalytic mixture model by integrating over posterior draws of individual antibody concentrations, allowing joint inference on latent serostate membership, force of infection, and serological waning rate. We applied the framework to three cross-sectional serosurveys of the population of England, for enteroviruses A71 (EV-A71) and D68 (EV-D68) and coxsackievirus A6 (CVA6), which are leading causes of severe respiratory illness and hand, foot, and mouth disease. We estimated consistently higher and more persistent lifetime antibody concentrations for EV-D68 than for EV-A71 and CVA6. The proportion of recently infected individuals peaks around 40% by age 5 years for CVA6 and around 32% by age 7 years for EV-A71, before declining with age. These estimates are conditional on a model structure excluding complete seroreversion, which, where identifiable, implied a half-life of several decades. For EV-D68, the inferred proportion previously infected exceeded 50% by age 13 years and grew, with the force of infection declining more gradually with age. These estimates differ from those previously obtained from binarised versions of the same data. Our framework uncovers the wide-ranging variation in antibody levels that are often obscured by conventional endpoint titre methods and infers infection rates directly from raw titration data, without dichotomising at predetermined seropositivity cut-offs, while making minimal assumptions about virus-specific infection mechanisms. Author summary Serological tests measure antibody levels to estimate virus spread and protection from infection (immunity). Virus neutralisation assays dilute serum samples in steps and mix them with virus and cell cultures. The antibody titre is the highest dilution at which cells are protected from infection. Traditional analyses discard much of the testing information and overlook test imperfections. We present a two-part Bayesian framework that estimates antibody concentrations from the raw dilution data, carries the resulting uncertainty forward, and infers age-specific transmission of three common viruses – EV-A71, EV-D68, and CVA6. Our results show that EV-D68 infections may be more common, especially in children, than the other two viruses. This approach gives a clearer picture of seroconversion dynamics without dichotomising samples at fixed thresholds and has potential to improve estimation of virus transmission and population susceptibility.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of conventional serological methods in estimating infection risk patterns by introducing a Bayesian framework that accounts for uncertainty in virus neutralisation assay titration data.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The framework was applied to three cross-sectional serosurveys of the population of England, focusing on enteroviruses A71 (EV-A71) and D68 (EV-D68) and coxsackievirus A6 (CVA6).
analysis.methods: The study introduced a two-part Bayesian framework: first, a mechanistic model to estimate antibody concentrations from raw titration data while quantifying uncertainty, and second, an age-structured sero-catalytic mixture model that integrates over posterior draws of individual antibody concentrations to infer latent serostate membership, force of infection, and serological waning rate.
analysis.main_results: The framework estimated consistently higher and more persistent lifetime antibody concentrations for EV-D68 compared to EV-A71 and CVA6. The proportion of recently infected individuals peaked around 40% by age 5 years for CVA6 and around 32% by age 7 years for EV-A71, then declined with age. For EV-D68, the inferred proportion previously infected exceeded 50% by age 13 years, with a gradual decline in force of infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results show that EV-D68 infections may be more common, especially in children, than the other two viruses. The framework provides a more accurate estimation of seroconversion dynamics by avoiding dichotomisation at fixed seropositivity thresholds.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform improved estimation of virus transmission and population susceptibility, offering a more nuanced understanding of infection patterns and immunity dynamics for EV-A71, EV-D68, and CVA6.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The estimates are conditional on a model structure excluding complete seroreversion, which may limit generalisability. The evidence strength is moderate, as the framework relies on assumptions about antibody dynamics and requires further validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a Bayesian framework to estimate latent infection risk patterns from virus neutralisation assay titration data, addressing the limitations of traditional interpolation-based methods that neglect uncertainty. The framework was applied to three cross-sectional serosurveys in England focusing on EV-A71, EV-D68, and CVA6, which are leading causes of severe respiratory illness and hand, foot, and mouth disease. The results show that EV-D68 infections may be more common in children than the other two viruses, with higher and more persistent antibody concentrations. The study highlights the importance of considering antibody dynamics and uncertainty in serological analysis, offering a more accurate estimation of seroconversion dynamics without dichotomising samples at fixed thresholds. However, the estimates are conditional on excluding seroreversion, which may limit generalisability. The evidence strength is moderate, as the framework relies on assumptions about antibody dynamics and requires further validation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过引入一种考虑病毒中和试验滴度数据中不确定性的贝叶斯框架,解决传统血清学方法在估计感染风险模式方面的局限性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该框架应用于英格兰人口的三项横断面血清流行调查,重点关注A71型肠道病毒(EV-A71)、D68型肠道病毒(EV-D68)和A6型柯萨奇病毒(CVA6)。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究引入了一种两部分的贝叶斯框架:首先,一个机制模型用于从原始滴度数据中估计抗体浓度并量化不确定性;其次,一个年龄结构化的血清催化混合模型,通过整合个体抗体浓度的后验抽样,推断潜在的血清状态归属、感染力和血清学衰减率。
elements_zh.main_results: 该框架估计EV-D68的终身抗体浓度比EV-A71和CVA6更高且更持久。近期感染个体的比例在CVA6中,5岁时达到约40%;在EV-A71中,7岁时达到约32%,随后随年龄增长而下降。对于EV-D68,估计的先前感染比例在13岁时超过50%,并且感染力随年龄增长而逐渐下降。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,EV-D68的感染可能比另外两种病毒更为常见,尤其是在儿童中。该框架通过避免在固定血清阳性阈值处对样本进行二元化处理,提供了对血清转换动态更准确的估计。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以用于改进病毒感染率和人群易感性的估计,为EV-A71、EV-D68和CVA6的感染模式及免疫动态提供更细致的理解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这些估计基于一个排除完全血清逆转的模型结构,这可能限制其推广性。证据强度中等,因为该框架依赖于关于抗体动态的假设,并需要进一步验证。

The proportion of recently infected individuals peaked around 40% by age 5 years for CVA6 and around 32% by age 7 years for EV-A71, then declined with age. For EV-D68, the inferred proportion previously infected exceeded 50% by age 13 years, with a gradual decline in force of infection.

papers.title_zh: 一种基于贝叶斯建模的框架,用于从病毒中和试验滴度数据中推断潜在感染风险模式
papers.source_body_en: Serological assays remain the standard approach for estimating the cumulative incidence of a pathogen and monitoring population immunity. Titration data from virus neutralisation assays are conventionally analysed using a nearly century-old interpolation-based method that neglects inherent imperfections in the assay and produces estimates with no measure of uncertainty. We introduce a two-part Bayesian framework for inferring latent infection risk directly from raw titration data. First, we develop a mechanistic model for serum antibody titration data that estimates antibody concentrations while quantifying uncertainty. Second, we propagate this uncertainty into an age-structured sero-catalytic mixture model by integrating over posterior draws of individual antibody concentrations, allowing joint inference on latent serostate membership, force of infection, and serological waning rate. We applied the framework to three cross-sectional serosurveys of the population of England, for enteroviruses A71 (EV-A71) and D68 (EV-D68) and coxsackievirus A6 (CVA6), which are leading causes of severe respiratory illness and hand, foot, and mouth disease. We estimated consistently higher and more persistent lifetime antibody concentrations for EV-D68 than for EV-A71 and CVA6. The proportion of recently infected individuals peaks around 40% by age 5 years for CVA6 and around 32% by age 7 years for EV-A71, before declining with age. These estimates are conditional on a model structure excluding complete seroreversion, which, where identifiable, implied a half-life of several decades. For EV-D68, the inferred proportion previously infected exceeded 50% by age 13 years and grew, with the force of infection declining more gradually with age. These estimates differ from those previously obtained from binarised versions of the same data. Our framework uncovers the wide-ranging variation in antibody levels that are often obscured by conventional endpoint titre methods and infers infection rates directly from raw titration data, without dichotomising at predetermined seropositivity cut-offs, while making minimal assumptions about virus-specific infection mechanisms. Author summary Serological tests measure antibody levels to estimate virus spread and protection from infection (immunity). Virus neutralisation assays dilute serum samples in steps and mix them with virus and cell cultures. The antibody titre is the highest dilution at which cells are protected from infection. Traditional analyses discard much of the testing information and overlook test imperfections. We present a two-part Bayesian framework that estimates antibody concentrations from the raw dilution data, carries the resulting uncertainty forward, and infers age-specific transmission of three common viruses – EV-A71, EV-D68, and CVA6. Our results show that EV-D68 infections may be more common, especially in children, than the other two viruses. This approach gives a clearer picture of seroconversion dynamics without dichotomising samples at fixed thresholds and has potential to improve estimation of virus transmission and population susceptibility.
papers.abstract_zh: 血清学检测仍然是估计病原体累积感染率和监测人群免疫力的标准方法。病毒中和试验的滴度数据通常使用一种近一个世纪的插值方法进行分析,这种方法忽略了试验本身固有的不完美性,并且产生的估计值没有不确定性度量。我们引入了一种两部分的贝叶斯框架,直接从原始滴度数据中推断潜在的感染风险模式。首先,我们开发了一个机制模型,用于估计血清抗体滴度数据中的抗体浓度,并量化不确定性。其次,我们将这种不确定性传播到一个年龄结构化的血清催化混合模型中,通过整合个体抗体浓度的后验抽样,实现对潜在血清状态归属、感染力和血清学衰减率的联合推断。我们将该框架应用于英格兰人口的三项横断面血清流行调查,调查对象包括引起严重呼吸道疾病和手足口病的主要病原体——A71型肠道病毒(EV-A71)、D68型肠道病毒(EV-D68)和A6型柯萨奇病毒(CVA6)。我们估计EV-D68的终身抗体浓度比EV-A71和CVA6更高且更持久。对于CVA6,近期感染个体的比例在5岁时达到约40%,对于EV-A71则在7岁时达到约32%,随后随年龄增长而下降。这些估计基于一个排除完全血清逆转的模型结构,该结构在可识别的情况下暗示了抗体的半衰期为数十年。对于EV-D68,估计的先前感染比例在13岁时超过50%,并且感染力随年龄增长而逐渐下降。这些估计与之前从相同数据二元化版本中获得的结果不同。我们的框架揭示了抗体水平的广泛变化,这些变化通常被传统终点滴度方法所掩盖,并且直接从原始滴度数据中推断感染率,而无需在预设的血清阳性阈值处进行二元化处理,同时对病毒特异性感染机制做出最少假设。作者摘要 血清学检测通过测量抗体水平来估计病毒传播情况和感染保护(免疫力)。病毒中和试验通过逐步稀释血清样本,并将其与病毒和细胞培养物混合来检测抗体水平。抗体滴度是细胞在何种最高稀释度下仍能被保护免受感染的度量。传统分析方法忽略了试验中的许多信息,并未考虑试验本身的不完美性。我们提出了一种两部分的贝叶斯框架,该框架从原始稀释数据中估计抗体浓度,将由此产生的不确定性向前传递,并直接从原始滴度数据中推断三种常见病毒——EV-A71、EV-D68和CVA6的年龄特异性感染率。我们的研究结果表明,EV-D68的感染可能比另外两种病毒更为常见,尤其是在儿童中。这种方法避免了在固定阈值处对样本进行二元化处理,从而更清晰地描绘了血清转换的动态过程,具有改进病毒感染率和人群易感性估计的潜力。
papers.summary_zh: 血清学检测仍然是估计病原体累积感染率和监测人群免疫力的标准方法。病毒中和试验的滴度数据通常使用一种近一个世纪的插值方法进行分析,这种方法忽略了试验本身固有的不完美性,并且产生的估计值没有不确定性度量。我们引入了一种两部分的贝叶斯框架,直接从原始滴度数据中推断潜在的感染风险模式。首先,我们开发了一个机制模型,用于估计血清抗体滴度数据中的抗体浓度,并量化不确定性。其次,我们将这种不确定性传播到一个年龄结构化的血清催化混合模型中,通过整合个体抗体浓度的后验抽样,实现对潜在血清状态归属、感染力和血清学衰减率的联合推断。我们将该框架应用于英格兰人口的三项横断面血清流行调查,调查对象包括引起严重呼吸道疾病和手足口病的主要病原体——A71型肠道病毒(EV-A71)、D68型肠道病毒(EV-D68)和A6型柯萨奇病毒(CVA6)。我们估计EV-D68的终身抗体浓度比EV-A71和CVA6更高且更持久。对于CVA6,近期感染个体的比例在5岁时达到约40%,对于EV-A71则在7岁时达到约32%,随后随年龄增长而下降。这些估计基于一个排除完全血清逆转的模型结构,该结构在可识别的情况下暗示了抗体的半衰期为数十年。对于EV-D68,估计的先前感染比例在13岁时超过50%,并且感染力随年龄增长而逐渐下降。这些估计与之前从相同数据二元化版本中获得的结果不同。我们的框架揭示了抗体水平的广泛变化,这些变化通常被传统终点滴度方法所掩盖,并且直接从原始滴度数据中推断感染率,而无需在预设的血清阳性阈值处进行二元化处理,同时对病毒特异性感染机制做出最少假设。作者摘要 血清学检测通过测量抗体水平来估计病毒传播情况和感染保护(免疫力)。病毒中和试验通过逐步稀释血清样本,并将其与病毒和细胞培养物混合来检测抗体水平。抗体滴度是细胞在何种最高稀释度下仍能被保护免受感染的度量。传统分析方法忽略了试验中的许多信息,并未考虑试验本身的不完美性。我们提出了一种两部分的贝叶斯框架,该框架从原始稀释数据中估计抗体浓度,将由此产生的不确定性向前传递,并直接从原始滴度数据中推断三种常见病毒——EV-A71、EV-D68和CVA6的年龄特异性感染率。我们的研究结果表明,EV-D68的感染可能比另外两种病毒更为常见,尤其是在儿童中。这种方法避免了在固定阈值处对样本进行二元化处理,从而更清晰地描绘了血清转换的动态过程,具有改进病毒感染率和人群易感性估计的潜力。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过引入一种考虑病毒中和试验滴度数据中不确定性的贝叶斯框架,解决传统血清学方法在估计感染风险模式方面的局限性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该框架应用于英格兰人口的三项横断面血清流行调查,重点关注A71型肠道病毒(EV-A71)、D68型肠道病毒(EV-D68)和A6型柯萨奇病毒(CVA6)。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究引入了一种两部分的贝叶斯框架:首先,一个机制模型用于从原始滴度数据中估计抗体浓度并量化不确定性;其次,一个年龄结构化的血清催化混合模型,通过整合个体抗体浓度的后验抽样,推断潜在的血清状态归属、感染力和血清学衰减率。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该框架估计EV-D68的终身抗体浓度比EV-A71和CVA6更高且更持久。近期感染个体的比例在CVA6中,5岁时达到约40%;在EV-A71中,7岁时达到约32%,随后随年龄增长而下降。对于EV-D68,估计的先前感染比例在13岁时超过50%,并且感染力随年龄增长而逐渐下降。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,EV-D68的感染可能比另外两种病毒更为常见,尤其是在儿童中。该框架通过避免在固定血清阳性阈值处对样本进行二元化处理,提供了对血清转换动态更准确的估计。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以用于改进病毒感染率和人群易感性的估计,为EV-A71、EV-D68和CVA6的感染模式及免疫动态提供更细致的理解。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这些估计基于一个排除完全血清逆转的模型结构,这可能限制其推广性。证据强度中等,因为该框架依赖于关于抗体动态的假设,并需要进一步验证。

papers.title: Identification of Novel Acylthiourea-Based PROTACs Exhibiting Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Activity against Enteroviruses
papers.abstract: Abstract Enteroviruses are the primary cause of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD). The absence of broad-spectrum antivirals, due to high serotypic and genetic diversity, greatly hampers effective treatment. In this study, we developed a novel type of acylthiourea-based proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) to induce targeted protein degradation. Compound X14 was identified as a potent candidate. X14 showed strong anti-EV71 activity by inhibiting viral replication. It directly binds to the EV71 3D polymerase with higher affinity than ribavirin and causes proteasome-dependent degradation of the 3D protein. X14 demonstrated broad-spectrum activity against representative EV-A, EV-B, EV-C, and EV-D enteroviruses and exhibited superior in vivo efficacy compared to the parent compound. X14 is a PROTAC targeting EV71 3D polymerase, making it a promising antiviral candidate and chemical tool for HFMD.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决由于肠道病毒高度的血清型和遗传多样性导致的缺乏针对肠道病毒的广谱抗病毒药物,这极大地阻碍了HFMD的有效治疗。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及开发基于酰基硫脲的蛋白降解靶向嵌合体(PROTACs),以靶向肠道病毒的3D聚合酶,重点研究EV71。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员开发了一种新型基于酰基硫脲的PROTACs,并鉴定出化合物X14作为有前景的候选物。X14被测试其对EV71的抗病毒活性以及对多种肠道病毒的广谱抗病毒药物活性。
elements_zh.main_results: 化合物X14通过抑制病毒复制显示出强效的抗EV71活性,并对代表性的EV-A、EV-B、EV-C和EV-D肠道病毒表现出广谱活性。它还显示出优于母体化合物的体内疗效。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释认为,X14直接与EV71 3D聚合酶结合,其亲和力高于利巴韦林,并导致3D蛋白的蛋白酶体依赖性降解,使其成为HFMD的有前景的抗病毒药物候选物和化学工具。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,X14可能成为肠道病毒感染(特别是EV71)治疗的有价值的工具,并有助于开发更有效的抗病毒药物策略用于HFMD。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括缺乏随机对照试验以及需要进一步的体内和临床验证。由于缺乏长期疗效和安全性数据,证据强度中等。

CDC's Wastewater Monitoring Program Explore This Topic Search Search Clear Search For Everyone CDC's Wastewater Program About Wastewater Data Common Respiratory Viruses Emerging Viruses Stories Communication Resources View all search clear search Wastewater Monitoring Menu clear search For Everyone CDC's Wastewater Program About Wastewater Data Common Respiratory Viruses Emerging Viruses Stories Communication Resources View All Home CDC's Wastewater Program About Wastewater Data Common Respiratory Viruses Emerging Viruses Stories Communication Resources View Menu Wastewater Monitoring Centers of Excellence For Everyone Sept. 23, 2026, visit link for details. Español What to know CDC's Wastewater Monitoring Centers of Excellence serve as regional leaders in wastewater monitoring implementation and coordination. They foster innovation, develop and conduct trainings, and provide technical assistance to jurisdictions. About Centers of Excellence Public health departments lead the Wastewater Monitoring Centers of Excellence, which are located in California, Colorado, Houston, New York, North Carolina, and Wisconsin. The Centers of Excellence advance their mission through collaborative partnerships with academic and utility partners. The Epidemiology and Laboratory Capacity for the Prevention and Control of Emerging Infectious Diseases (ELC) cooperative agreement competitively selected and funded the sites. Locations Learn more about the Centers of Excellence View information about each Center and how they support wastewater monitoring across the United States. View by location California Colorado Houston New York North Carolina Wisconsin California The California Department of Public Health leads the California Center of Excellence in partnership with Stanford University and Emory University. They support the following states and territories: Alaska, American Samoa, Arizona, California, Federated States of Micronesia, Guam, Hawaii, Idaho, Marshall Islands, Nevada, Northern Mariana Islands, Oregon, Palau, and Washington. For more information about California's work, visit California Wastewater Surveillance Center of Excellence. Back to Top of Learn more about the Centers of Excellence Colorado The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment leads the Colorado Center of Excellence in partnership with the University of Denver. They support the following states: Colorado, Iowa, Kansas, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, North Dakota, Utah, South Dakota, and Wyoming. For more information about Colorado's work, visit Colorado National Wastewater Surveillance System Center of Excellence. Spotlight The Colorado Center of Excellence conducted an evaluation of wastewater monitoring data to monitor enterovirus D68 (EV-D68), a virus that typically causes respiratory illness, ranging from mild (like a common cold) to much more severe. Wastewater monitoring served as an early warning system, detecting infections up to a month before clinical testing. The Colorado Center of Excellence is using this data to prepare healthcare facilities for potential surges during the respiratory virus season. Back to Top of Learn more about the Centers of Excellence Houston The Houston Health Department leads the Houston Center of Excellence in partnership with Rice University. They support the following states and localities: Arkansas, the District of Columbia, Chicago, Houston, Louisiana, Los Angeles County, Maricopa County, New Mexico, New York City, Oklahoma, Philadelphia, and Texas. For more information about Houston's work, visit Houston Wastewater Epidemiology. Spotlight The Houston Center of Excellence is empowering K-12 school staff, students, and families to make data-informed decisions by providing school-level wastewater monitoring data via text. This helps public health officials and individuals know whether COVID-19, influenza, and/or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are circulating within a school. Health and school officials have used this information to plan vaccination clinics at the school, which have also offered opportunities for students to catch up on other missed vaccinations. Back to Top of Learn more about the Centers of Excellence New York The New York Health Department leads the New York Center of Excellence in partnership with Syracuse University. They support the following states and territories: Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Puerto Rico, Rhode Island, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Vermont. For more information about New York’s work, visit NYS Wastewater Surveillance CoE and New York State Wastewater Surveillance. Back to Top of Learn more about the Centers of Excellence North Carolina The North Carolina Health Department leads the North Carolina Center of Excellence in partnership with University of North Carolina-Chapel Hill. They support the following states: Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Tennessee. Back to Top of Learn more about the Centers of Excellence Wisconsin The Wisconsin Department of Health Services leads the Wisconsin Center of Excellence in partnership with the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee. They support the following states: Delaware, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Wisconsin, and West Virginia. For more information about Wisconsin's work, visit Wisconsin Wastewater Monitoring Program. Español What to know CDC's Wastewater Monitoring Centers of Excellence serve as regional leaders in wastewater monitoring implementation and coordination. They foster innovation, develop and conduct trainings, and provide technical assistance to jurisdictions. About Centers of Excellence Public health departments lead the Wastewater Monitoring Centers of Excellence, which are located in California, Colorado, Houston, New York, North Carolina, and Wisconsin. The Centers of Excellence advance their mission through collaborative partnerships with academic and utility partners. The Epidemiology and Laboratory Capacity for the Prevention and Control of Emerging Infectious Diseases (ELC) cooperative agreement competitively selected and funded the sites. Locations Learn more about the Centers of Excellence View information about each Center and how they support wastewater monitoring across the United States. View by location California Colorado Houston New York North Carolina Wisconsin California The California Department of Public Health leads the California Center of Excellence in partnership with Stanford University and Emory University. They support the following states and territories: Alaska, American Samoa, Arizona, California, Federated States of Micronesia, Guam, Hawaii, Idaho, Marshall Islands, Nevada, Northern Mariana Islands, Oregon, Palau, and Washington. For more information about California's work, visit California Wastewater Surveillance Center of Excellence. Back to Top of Learn more about the Centers of Excellence Colorado The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment leads the Colorado Center of Excellence in partnership with the University of Denver. They support the following states: Colorado, Iowa, Kansas, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, North Dakota, Utah, South Dakota, and Wyoming. For more information about Colorado's work, visit Colorado National Wastewater Surveillance System Center of Excellence. Spotlight The Colorado Center of Excellence conducted an evaluation of wastewater monitoring data to monitor enterovirus D68 (EV-D68), a virus that typically causes respiratory illness, ranging from mild (like a common cold) to much more severe. Wastewater monitoring served as an early warning system, detecting infections up to a month before clinical testing. The Colorado Center of Excellence is using this data to prepare healthcare facilities for potential surges during the respiratory virus season. Back to Top of Learn more about the Centers of Excellence Houston The Houston Health Department leads the Houston Center of Excellence in partnership with Rice University. They support the following states and localities: Arkansas, the District of Columbia, Chicago, Houston, Louisiana, Los Angeles County, Maricopa County, New Mexico, New York City, Oklahoma, Philadelphia, and Texas. For more information about Houston's work, visit Houston Wastewater Epidemiology. Spotlight The Houston Center of Excellence is empowering K-12 school staff, students, and families to make data-informed decisions by providing school-level wastewater monitoring data via text. This helps public health officials and individuals know whether COVID-19, influenza, and/or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are circulating within a school. Health and school officials have used this information to plan vaccination clinics at the school, which have also offered opportunities for students to catch up on other missed vaccinations. Back to Top of Learn more about the Centers of Excellence New York The New York Health Department leads the New York Center of Excellence in partnership with Syracuse University. They support the following states and territories: Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Puerto Rico, Rhode Island, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Vermont. For more information about New York’s work, visit NYS Wastewater Surveillance CoE and New York State Wastewater Surveillance. Back to Top of Learn more about the Centers of Excellence North Carolina The North Carolina Health Department leads the North Carolina Center of Excellence in partnership with University of North Carolina-Chapel Hill. They support the following states: Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Tennessee. Back to Top of Learn more about the Centers of Excellence Wisconsin The Wisconsin Department of Health Services leads the Wisconsin Center of Excellence in partnership with the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee. They support the following states: Delaware, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Wisconsin, and West Virginia. For more information about Wisconsin's work, visit Wisconsin Wastewater Monitoring Program. analysis.brief_en: The CDC's Wastewater Monitoring Centers of Excellence are regional leaders in implementing and coordinating wastewater monitoring programs to detect and respond to enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) and other pathogens. These centers, located in California, Colorado, Houston, New York, North Carolina, and Wisconsin, support multiple states and territories, including Alaska, American Samoa, Arizona, and others. They use wastewater data as an early warning system, detecting infections up to a month before clinical testing, which helps prepare healthcare facilities for potential surges during the respiratory virus season. The program also empowers K-12 school staff, students, and families with data-informed decisions about the circulation of viruses like COVID-19, influenza, and RSV. The Centers of Excellence collaborate with academic and utility partners, and their work includes training, technical assistance, and fostering innovation in public health responses. The CDC's Wastewater Monitoring Program is actively involved in these efforts, with ongoing activities to enhance surveillance and preparedness.

elements_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 废水监测被用于在临床检测前一个月检测感染,这有助于医疗机构为呼吸道病毒季节期间可能出现的病例激增做好准备。该计划还支持学校基于数据做出关于如新冠病毒(COVID-19)、流感和呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)等病毒传播情况的决策。
elements_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 卓越中心正在积极进行评估,提供技术援助,并推动废水监测方面的创新。它们还参与培训和支持各地区,持续开展活动以增强公共卫生应对能力。

news.title_zh: 废水监测卓越中心 - 疾病控制与预防中心 | CDC (.gov)
news.source_body_en: The CDC's Wastewater Monitoring Centers of Excellence are regional leaders in implementing and coordinating wastewater monitoring programs to detect and respond to enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) and other pathogens. These centers, located in California, Colorado, Houston, New York, North Carolina, and Wisconsin, support multiple states and territories, including Alaska, American Samoa, Arizona, and others. They use wastewater data as an early warning system, detecting infections up to a month before clinical testing, which helps prepare healthcare facilities for potential surges during the respiratory virus season. The program also empowers K-12 school staff, students, and families with data-informed decisions about the circulation of viruses like COVID-19, influenza, and RSV. The Centers of Excellence collaborate with academic and utility partners, and their work includes training, technical assistance, and fostering innovation in public health responses. The CDC's Wastewater Monitoring Program is actively involved in these efforts, with ongoing activities to enhance surveillance and preparedness.
news.content_zh: 疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)的废水监测卓越中心在实施和协调废水监测计划以检测和应对肠道病毒D68(EV-D68)及其他病原体方面处于区域领先地位。这些中心位于加利福尼亚州、科罗拉多州、休斯顿、纽约州、北卡罗来纳州和威斯康星州,支持多个州和领地,包括阿拉斯加、美属萨摩亚、亚利桑那州等。他们利用废水数据作为早期预警系统,能够在临床检测前一个月检测到感染,从而帮助医疗机构为呼吸道病毒季节期间可能出现的病例激增做好准备。该计划还使K-12学校工作人员、学生和家庭能够基于数据做出关于如新冠病毒(COVID-19)、流感和呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)等病毒传播情况的决策。卓越中心与学术界和公用事业合作伙伴协作,其工作包括培训、技术援助以及推动公共卫生应对措施的创新。CDC的废水监测计划积极参与这些努力,持续开展活动以增强监测和应对能力。
